items.summary: The delay in refunding ₹53 crore to Vodafone Idea Limited paints a “grim picture” of the Department’s handling of tax refunds, the Delhi High Court recently observed while ordering refund of the amount to the telecom operator [Vodafone Idea Vs ACIT]. A bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Rajneesh Kumar Gupta held that once a refund arises from an assessment or an appellate order, it becomes a vested and crystallised right of the assessee. “ The case in hands portrays a grim picture of the state of affairs prevailing in the Department so far as issues relating to refund is concerned ,” the Court said in its judgment of August 18. The Court directed the Department to pay Vodafone Idea ₹53 crore along with interest by September 30. If the amount is not credited by the deadline, it will carry additional interest at 1 percent per month over and above the statutory interest, the Court ordered. Justice Dinesh Mehta and Justice Rajneesh Kumar Gupta The dispute concerned assessment years 2003-04 and 2008-09 to 2013-14. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that after 6 weeks, the government can clear the land with the help of the police. "The appellants shall vacate the dwelling in the three jhuggi jhopris within six weeks from today. And within this period, they shall be provided with the accommodations allotted to them in DUSIB Colony. Whereafter, they shall be evicted to clear the land, if necessary, with the assistance of the police," the Court ordered. It ruled that there had been no violation of the rehabilitation policy in moving the residents in this case. items.title: Heritage, architecture, and a silk museum: The rail trail from Bengaluru to Kolar
items.summary: Destination fatigue had set in. Weary of the regular tourist spots within driving distance on the outskirts of Bengaluru, I embarked on an off-the-beaten track destination, scouting new experiences and experiential travel. My exploration spree covered a bunch of quaint, British-era railway stations built on an 81-km narrow gauge line built between Bengaluru and Kolar. Currently it is a broad gauge line but the old stations have survived. The heritage route covers four distinct stations, beginning at Doddajala, winding through Devanahalli and Avatihalli, and culminating at the Nandi station against the backdrop of the charming Nandi hills. These stations have been painstakingly restored from their crumbling conditions by INTACH Bengaluru in collaboration with South West Railway, using corporate social responsibility (CSR) funding from Mineral Enterprises Ltd and Discovery Village, and help from other communities and businesses. INTACH has ensured that the structure has adhered to the original vintage style.
